v0.8.0 made fufu work for a fleet of worktrees. What it did not do is get fufu invoked. fufu captures only when something calls it, and everything that calls it — an agent client's tool hook, a shell prompt, the repository's own pre-commit runner — sits outside fufu and has to be met on its own terms. This release is that boundary.

**One grammar for wiring, one for events**

`ff hook <agent|shell|editor> <install|uninstall|list|trigger> [name]` was a nested grammar over a flat set of facts. It collapses into two verbs a person types and one a client calls: `ff hook` and `ff unhook` take flat slugs — claude, codex, cursor, gemini, bash, zsh, fish — and `ff trigger <source>` is the machine surface. Bare `ff hook` reports what is on this machine and asks; `--all` skips the question, `-l` reports and stops.

The two namespaces differ on purpose. `hook` names a thing you integrate with; `trigger` names an event source, which is finer-grained — all three shell slugs install rc lines calling one `ff trigger shell`. The contracts differ to match: an unknown slug is a real error and a wiring failure is loud, while an unknown source exits 0 in silence, which is what makes a fufu trigger safe to wire into a client fufu has never heard of.

Codex, Cursor, and Gemini CLI join Claude Code. `crates/ff-cli/src/integ/` is one client-neutral core behind four thin protocol adapters, so what gets written is per-adapter rather than a user choice: a plugin directory fufu owns outright for Claude Code, merged entries in their own settings file for the others, marked rc lines for the shells. A line somebody wrote by hand is detected, reported, and never touched. `ff doctor` reads its wiring rows out of the same vector `ff hook -l` renders, so the two cannot disagree.

**A manual an agent can reach**

The once-per-session briefing is the only spelling lesson an agent gets, and it is capped by test because every session pays for it whether or not it needs it. That cap left everything past "commit, undo, don't write with git" nowhere to live: an agent needing `ff resolve`, `ff edit`, `ff lift`, or the difference between `ff undo` and `ff op revert` had no route to them, so it reached for `ff git rebase -i` and fought the model.

The two texts now split by what they cost. The briefing keeps the always-on contract and nothing else, coming down from 1,156 bytes to 667 with the budget lowered to 800 so the reduction is a contract rather than slack. Everything else moves to a skill fufu ships — the model, a recovery decision table, rewriting, held rewrites, parking, remotes, the landmines, the machine surface — which costs nothing until a client decides the situation calls for it, and names each verb's own `--help` as the authority rather than restating one.

Claude Code's skill rides inside the plugin fufu already owns; Codex takes a directory of its own. Cursor and Gemini read no skills directory and are not told to read one, because naming a manual that is not there is worse than saying nothing. For everywhere else — including clients fufu has never heard of, which the silent trigger exists to invite — `ff hook --skill` prints it verbatim to stdout, so `ff hook --skill > ~/.cursor/rules/fufu.md` produces a file byte-identical to the one an install writes. `ff --help` closes with a block telling an agent to run it, guarded with "SKIP if fufu's skill is already in your context", which is what makes an agent that was never briefed find the manual at all.

**Your hooks see the index populated**

Every hook-runner keyed on staging — lefthook, lint-staged, husky, the pre-commit framework — silently did nothing under `ff commit`. fufu keeps `.git/index` written to a tree, so during an open change it describes what the *last* commit took and `git diff --cached` is empty; lefthook's `{staged_files}` resolves to an empty list, every job is skipped, the runner exits 0, and the commit lands with nothing having run.

Git already does what is needed here: `commit -a` and `commit -- <path>` both populate the index before running `pre-commit`, and roll it back when the hook declines. So a close writes the index to the tree it is about to commit just before the first hook, and restores it byte-for-byte when the close does not land — byte-exact rather than a rewrite to HEAD's tree, because a user may have their own `git add` state and a refused close must not destroy it. A partial `ff commit <paths>` stages exactly what is landing, as git's pathspec form does, and a repository with no hooks pays two `stat` calls.

**`ff collide` answers one pair**

The verb shipped in v0.8.0 carrying two products and neither had an audience. The all-pairs matrix over every local branch was unreadable past a couple of dozen names, and the greedy clear set folded out of it existed to feed a scheduler fufu does not have. The sideways pitch — two people seeing each other before either has committed — was never available: open changes are read from a local ref namespace, so it reaches across worktrees on one machine and never across people.

`ff collide <other>` now compares the branch you are on against that one, and `ff collide <a> <b>` names both sides. The judging is unchanged; what went is the matrix and the ranking that fed it, and both performance cliffs went with it — 200 branches over a 5,000-file tree took two minutes, and 400 clear branches took 41.6s where two names is 5ms. The set-building belongs to tower: a verdict is a fact about two trees, and a set is a fact about a queue.

**Smaller things**

The ambient status-line channel is gone: `fufu.ambient` leaves the config registry and the code that rendered on it leaves the shell adapter. The prompt hook itself stays where it was and is now pure capture, which is what its zero-spawn budget always said it was.

Two clippy lints that arrived with Rust 1.98 are fixed: rust-toolchain.toml tracks stable, so a new stable is a new lint set and `-D warnings` turns that into a red main the day the runner image moves.

**Numbers**

9 commits over v0.8.0, +6,392/−2,622 across 46 files. 1,430 workspace tests, up from 1,364. 110 `ff explain` ids, up from 108.
